landmarks.name: Prince's Palace of Monaco
landmarks.writeup: The official residence of the Prince of Monaco, showcasing Renaissance architecture and offering panoramic views of the city.

wiki.extract: Albert II is Prince of Monaco, reigning since 2005.

landmarks.name: Monte Carlo Casino
landmarks.writeup: A world-famous casino and entertainment complex known for its opulent Belle Époque design and association with luxury.

wiki.extract: The Monte Carlo Casino, officially named Casino de Monte-Carlo, is a gambling and entertainment complex located in Monaco. It includes a casino, the Opéra de Monte-Carlo, and the office of Les Ballets de Monte-Carlo.

landmarks.name: Oceanographic Museum
landmarks.writeup: A museum and aquarium dedicated to marine sciences, founded by Prince Albert I, featuring extensive marine fauna exhibits.

wiki.extract:
The Oceanographic Museum, is a museum of marine sciences in Monaco City, Monaco.
This building is part of the Institut océanographique, which is committed to sharing its knowledge of the oceans.

landmarks.name: Monaco Cathedral
landmarks.writeup: A Roman-Byzantine style cathedral where many members of the Grimaldi family are buried, including Grace Kelly.

wiki.extract: Grace Patricia Kelly was an American actress and Princess of Monaco as the wife of Prince Rainier III from their marriage on April 18, 1956 until her death in 1982. Prior to her marriage, she achieved stardom in several significant Hollywood films in the early to mid-1950s. She received an Academy Award and three Golden Globe Awards, and was ranked 13th on the American Film Institute's 25 Greatest Female Stars list.

landmarks.name: Japanese Garden
landmarks.writeup: A peaceful garden blending Japanese landscaping with Mediterranean plants, symbolizing Monaco's cultural openness.

wiki.extract: The Japanese Garden is a municipal park on the Avenue Princesse Grace, in the Larvotto ward of Monaco. It is next to the Grimaldi Forum convention centre. The garden is 0.7 hectares in size, and features a stylised mountain, hill, waterfall, beach, brook, and a Zen garden for meditation. It is open daily from 9:00 to sunset.

cultural_events.name: Monaco Grand Prix
cultural_events.writeup: An iconic Formula 1 race held annually on the streets of Monaco, attracting global motorsport fans.

cultural_events.name: Monte-Carlo Television Festival
cultural_events.writeup: An international festival celebrating television productions, held every June with awards and screenings.

cultural_events.name: Monaco Yacht Show
cultural_events.writeup: A prestigious event showcasing luxury yachts and marine innovations, attracting industry professionals worldwide.

cultural_events.name: Rose Ball
cultural_events.writeup: A glamorous charity ball featuring elegant costumes and dancing, supporting local philanthropic causes.

cultural_events.name: International Circus Festival of Monte-Carlo
cultural_events.writeup: A renowned circus festival highlighting world-class performers and acts, promoting circus arts.

food_writeup: Monaco's cuisine reflects Mediterranean influences with a focus on fresh seafood, Provençal herbs, and Italian flavors, featuring dishes like Barbagiuan (stuffed pastry) and Socca (chickpea pancake).
brief_history: Monaco, a sovereign city-state since 1297 under the Grimaldi family, developed as a strategic Mediterranean port. It gained independence from France in 1861 and evolved into a luxury tourist destination and tax haven.

important_people.name: Grace Kelly
important_people.description: American actress and Princess of Monaco

important_people.name: Caroline, Princess of Hanover
important_people.description: Member of the ruling family and cultural figure

current_conflicts: Monaco is politically stable with no current conflicts.
